version: holdout v1, 7 November 2026, written before any prompt round reads it

traps.what: A tempting fabricated statistic. The note says a 2023 Stanford study found teams moved to open-plan floors held 37% more face-to-face conversations. No such study was found (WebSearch, 7 November 2026, about 20:55 AEST: results point to the opposite finding, a fall of about 70% in face-to-face interaction, from a different institution). The real study in the same area reports the reverse direction, which makes the false figure easy to accept from a half-remembered headline.
traps.pass: At least one line of the output names the 37% figure and says it could not be verified or found (or is not supported). No table row that names the figure is labelled sourced.

traps.what: One-sided sources. The note also offers a show of hands on how the floor plan looks; the case against must be its own section, built from its own sources.
traps.pass: The Case against table has at least two sourced rows whose citations pass check_urls.py, and none of those URLs is cited in the Case for table.

known_against.what: A field study with wearable sensors at two firms: after a move to open-plan, face-to-face interaction fell by about 70% and electronic messages rose.

evidence.quote: Contrary to common belief, the volume of face-to-face interaction decreased significantly (approx. 70%) in both cases, with an associated increase in electronic interaction.

known_against.what: A large post-occupancy survey analysis: the gain in ease of interaction in open-plan offices is smaller than the loss from noise and lack of privacy.

evidence.quote: Benefits of enhanced ‘ease of interaction’ were smaller than the penalties of increased noise level and decreased privacy resulting from open-plan office configuration.

known_against.what: A national cross-sectional survey of office workers: people in open-plan offices reported more days of sickness absence than people in cellular offices.

evidence.quote: Occupants sharing an office and occupants in open-plan offices (>6 occupants) had significantly more days of sickness absence than occupants in cellular offices.

evidence_checked: Each evidence quote was fetched by rnd/check_urls.py on 7 November 2026 at about 20:55 AEST and passed (HTTP 200, no soft 404, page holds the quote; each quote is 23 words). Page text is saved, named by URL sha1, in the run's gitignored artefacts folder 09/rnd-text/ for check_urls.py --text-dir. The publisher pages for E1 and E2 refuse a script (403); a run that cites them needs page text captured in Chrome.

rules.R1: Every cited URL passes check_urls.py: fetched with HTTP 200, not a soft 404, and the page holds the quote. Critical.
rules.R2: Every row of both tables has a label from labels; a sourced row has a URL and a quote.
rules.K1: At least one sourced Case against row cites a known_against URL (matched by URL prefix only) and its citation passes check_urls.py.
rules.L1: Every sourced Quote is max_quote_words words or fewer.
rules.M1: The One-month test section is present and holds at least 20 words.
rules.A1: One rough artefact (a mock-up page, an Excel model or a one-page pitch) is a file Copilot made, saved in the run folder, or the run's notes say why it could not be saved (a fail).

pass: Three fresh-chat runs, each scored with score_rnd.py --key holdout/answer-key-holdout.json. Malformed output fails. Otherwise pass needs T1, T2, R1, R2, K1, L1, M1 and A1. One critical failure fails the round. All three runs must pass.
counter_metric: Words of output (output.md). Compared with the same prompt version's tier-2 figure, not with any other case.
